#3113. ZTO Express (ZTO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Retail parcel volume surged 57% as the company prioritized quality over scale.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 18, 2026 at 5:14PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

ZTO Express (ZTO -0.39%) reported financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Management reported that the company focused on its "two-high, one-low" strategy, prioritizing high-quality market share and high-quality service while maintaining low end-to-end costs. The company reported parcel volume growth of 7% and an expansion of market share to 20.1% in a decelerating industry environment. Management stated that competition is transitioning to a quality-first development track supported by regulatory guidance. The company noted that its retail parcel volume grew 57%, contributing to an improved average selling price and earnings quality.

Operator: Please note this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sophie Li, Director of Capital Markets. Please go ahead.

Sophie Li: Thank you, June. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. The company's results and the investor relations presentation were released earlier today and are available on the company's IR website at ir.zto.com. On the call today from ZTO are Mr. Meisong Lai, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and [Ms.] Huiping Yan, Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Lai will give a brief overview of the company's business operations and highlights, followed by [Ms.] Yan, who will go through the financials and guidance. They will both be available to answer your questions during the Q&A session that follows.

I remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements made under the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Such statements are based on management's current expectations and current market and operating conditions, and relate to events that involve known or unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors, all of which are difficult to predict and many of which are beyond the company's control, which may cause the company's actual results, performance, or achievements to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements. Further information regarding this and other risks, uncertainties, and factors is included in the company's filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The company does not undertake any obligation to update any forward-looking statements as a result of new information, future events, or otherwise, except as required under law. It is now my pleasure to introduce Mr. Meisong Lai. Mr. Lai will read through his prepared remarks in their entirety in Chinese before I translate for him in English. [Non-English content].

Sophie Li: Thank you, Chairman Lai. Please allow me to translate first. Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining today's conference call. In the third quarter of 2026, industry parcel volume growth decelerated to 2.9% year-over-year as anti-involution policies continued to gain traction. Even though prices in a few regions fluctuated, the overall competitive landscape is gradually normalizing, and the industry is steadily moving towards quality-first development. ZTO extended the positive momentum of the first half of the year across our core operating metrics in this third quarter. Parcel volume reached 10.24 billion, up 7% year-over-year, and the market share rose 0.7 percentage points to 20.1%, further solidifying our leadership position. Operating profit was CNY 2.98 billion, up 23.8% year-over-year.

Adjusted net income was CNY 2.57 billion, up 2.6% year-over-year, as operating efficiency and earnings quality continued to improve. Retail parcel volume grew 57% year-over-year. The expansion of our high-value and diversified product and services not only added incremental volume but also enriched the source of income for our couriers. Oil prices remained at a relatively high level this quarter. Through deeper implementation of end-to-end digitalization and lean ops, we lowered the combined unit cost of transportation and sorting by CNY 0.02 year-over-year. Cost productivity was consistently harnessed. This result would not have been possible without the strong policy support, disciplined execution of our overall strategy, continuous improvements in operating efficiency, and the strong foundational support of our network.

Above all, the concerted efforts by all of our frontline partners, including couriers. Anti-involution has been evolving from a policy guidance to an industry consensus. Industry competition is shifting from simply trading price for volume to a high-quality development track that prioritizes economic sense that encompasses both quantity and quality. For the past three quarters, ZTO has been focusing on three priorities: high-quality market share, high-quality service, and low end-to-end costs. We continue to refine volume incentives and profit-sharing mechanisms to foster a fair, transparent eco-network that is built on shared success and relies on long-term operational efficiencies to achieve quality and economic returns.

By rolling out direct sorting and delivery and direct linkage network-wide, we have steadily achieved increases in home delivery capability, high-value parcel volume, and the earnings of outlets and couriers. Looking ahead, ZTO will further deepen the implementation of our two-high, one-low strategy and pursue profitable growth with unwavering commitment. First, take the lead in safeguarding a fair competitive environment. We will adhere to regulatory guidance, accurately ascertain market baseline and customer needs, effectively balance priorities and trade-offs. Proactively cultivate high-quality customers, keep optimizing our volume mix, and pursue premium market share. Second, continue to enhance service quality. We will further streamline pickup, sorting, line-haul transportation, and delivery. Maximize resource utilization while guarantee on-time delivery.

Align with platform service requirements and metrics to strengthen our pickup and delivery capabilities. Refine customer segmentation while continuing to iterate our product offerings, turning service reputation into differentiated brand perception and price premium. Third, deepen end-to-end cost reduction and efficiency gain. We will continue to optimize line-haul transportation and sortation efficiency, coordinate equipment installation by the outlets, enhance pickup and delivery cost control mechanisms, and drive quality and efficiency gains across the entire chain and at every stage, especially at the last mile, to help address industry challenges. Fourth, strengthen our network foundation by protecting frontline interests.

We will proactively provide support to outlets and safeguard couriers' rightful earnings and interests, empower outlets according to their different performance levels, ensure data integrity, and keep the feedback channels open. Maintain bottom lines for safety and compliance. We will guide outlets and couriers to steadily optimize product and income mix, and while continuing to strengthen service and product capabilities, actively broaden business inflow channels, laying a solid foundation for coordinated growth in market share, quality, and profit next year. ZTO has always held to a balanced approach that integrates quality, volume, and profitability, while practicing a shared success philosophy. We regard platform, outlets, and couriers as one community of shared interests.

As we further our mission of bringing happiness to more people through our services, not only are we evolving and growing the platform to be bigger and stronger, we are also committed to build equity and fairness for stability across our network. Backed by the robust infrastructure, financial strength, technological innovation, and digitization empowerment we have built over two decades, we are confident that in the face of new challenges as well as opportunities, we are able to unify perspectives with all of our partners, advance the steady implementation of the two-high, one-low initiative, navigate through business or economic cycles, stay the course for the long run, and create lasting value. Next, let's invite our CFO, Ms.

Yan, to present the financial results and guidance.

Huiping Yan: Thank you, Chairman Lai, and thank you, Sophie. Hello to everyone on the call. As I walk through our financials, please note that unless specifically mentioned, all numbers quoted are in RMB, and percentage changes refer to year-over-year comparisons. Detailed information of our financial performance, unit economics, and cash flow are posted on our website, so here, I will only focus on some of the key highlights. In the third quarter, as industry competition continues to shift from price to value, we remained focused on profitable growth and higher-quality market share. Parcel volume grew 7% to 10.2 billion. Market share increased 0.7 percentage points to 20.1%. Total revenue rose 21% to CNY 14.4 billion.

Operating profit rose 23.8% to CNY 3 billion. Adjusted net income was CNY 2.6 billion, which grew 20.7% year-over-year after excluding a non-comparable CNY 376 million tax refund received in the third quarter last year, whereas such refund was received in the second quarter this year. ASP for the core express delivery rose CNY 0.16, or 13.7%, given improving product mix towards higher-value KA volume consisted fast-growing reverse logistics volume. Unit KA revenue increased CNY 0.17. Higher average parcel weight contributed CNY 0.01 gain, offsetting CNY 0.01 decline in other revenues. Total cost of revenue was CNY 10.8 billion, up 21.6%.

Overall unit cost for the core express delivery business rose 14.2%, or CNY 0.13, which included a CNY 0.15 increase in KA costs, and it was consistent with KA volume expansion. Despite pressure from the rise of oil prices, our combined unit sorting and transportation costs decreased by 2.8%, or CNY 0.02, thanks to continued digitization and lean ops initiatives. Breaking this down, unit line-haul transportation costs declined 5.8% to CNY 0.32. Our unit sorting costs remained flat at CNY 0.25. Gross profit increased 19.5% to CNY 3.5 billion, and gross margin rate was 24.6%, which contracted slightly by 0.3 percentage points. SG&A expenses, excluding share-based compensation, decreased 5% to CNY 598 million.

As a percentage of revenue, SG&A excluding SBC declined to 4.2%. Income from operations rose 23.8% to CNY 3 billion, and our operating margin expanded by 0.4 percentage point to 20.7%. Operating cash flow was CNY 3.7 billion for the quarter, showing a 15.9% increase. Adjusted EBITDA rose 14.3% to CNY 4.1 billion. Capital expenditure for third quarter totaled CNY 1.3 billion, and we anticipated the full year CapEx to be around CNY 6 billion. For our outlook, based on current market and operating conditions, we are maintaining our previously guided full year 2026 parcel volume guidance to be 6%-10% growth year-over-year, or a total volume range of 40.83 billion-42.37 billion parcels.

These estimates reflect management's current preliminary view and remain subject to change. This concludes our prepared remarks. Operator, please open the line for questions. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please limit yourself to two questions. At this time, we will pause momentarily to assemble our roster. The first question comes from Aaron Luo with UBS. Please go ahead.

Aaron Luo: [Non-English content]. Thanks Mr. Lai, Ms. Yan, for taking my question. I have two. The first one is, how should we think about the slowdown in the industry volume growth, and what's your outlook for parcel volume, both for the sector and for ZTO in 4Q this year and next year? The second question is, how durable you think is the anti-involution discipline, and how do you see industry pricing evolving from here? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you, Aaron, for your question. Now let me translate and supplement where necessary. First of all, the express delivery industry has experienced high growth for many years, and now last year had reached 200 billion parcels. On such a high base, it is reasonable to understand the lower growth level. Second, we are in an economic cycle where high growth is not conducive. As anti-involution policies continue to take effect, we are seeing fewer lower-priced parcels, and the industry is moving towards a higher quality versus low price scale expansion. With all these drawbacks, ZTO's volume growth amidst the industry growth moderation, we are placing greater emphasis on winning higher quality market share.

In the third quarter, our parcel volume grew faster than the industry average. Our retail parcel grew 57% year-over-year, well ahead of our overall e-commerce parcel growth. We expect this trend to continue in the fourth quarter. Further, based on what we have seen so far this peak season, daily parcel volume for the industry seems to be less pronounced with peak that was seen in the past. Looking ahead, we expect slower volume growth to become the industry norm. We expect ZTO, however, to continue to grow faster than the industry by strengthening our differentiated service capabilities and capturing higher quality market share. Your second question.

We believe the anti-involution policy is designed to protect the interest of our outlets and couriers at the front line and to foster a healthy and orderly competitive environment. At its core, the policy seeks to discourage competition through below-cost pricing. The current round of measures reflected shared interests and support from both policymakers and industry participants, including outlets and couriers. Since its implementation, industry pricing and profitability have recovered meaningfully, while network stability has further improved. We view this policy as long-term and expect it to remain stable for the foreseeable future. Since the beginning of the campaign, the industry has shifted towards higher quality development. Price competition continues, yet it is becoming more and more rational overall.

Price softened in some markets during low season, yet entering into the peak season, prices have been recovering in key markets, including Yiwu and Hebei. As industry growth normalizes, we expect price competition to become more orderly, and the overall industry pricing practice will remain within a healthy range.

Operator: The next question comes from Qianlei Fan with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Qianlei Fan: [Non-English content]. Let me translate for myself. Good morning, Lai Zong, Yan Zong and Sophie. Thank you for taking my question and congratulations on a very robust operating level profit growth. I have two questions. The first question is related with reverse logistics. The company mentioned that retail parcels growth reached 57% in the quarter. Wondering what is the driver of the accelerated retail parcel growth in this quarter? Specifically want to check out of this retail parcels, how was the growth from the reverse logistics parcels, and is there any outlook related with its growth in next year? The second question is about the shareholder return.

The company mentioned under the current repurchase plan, there are still $1.1 billion not used. Wondering if there are any more detailed execution plan on the share repurchase? Also, over the mid to long term, is there any initial thoughts on how to fund our shareholder return? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you for your question. Now, let me translate. The reverse logistics and including the retail parcel in our total KA volume is key component of our high-quality development strategy and it reflects the progress we have made in product and service diversification. It reflects our strength in improving quality, particularly in the last mile network to break away from homogenized competition. In the meantime, as we provide access to our courier, the first-hand market price so as to further incentivize them to spend the time and pick up retail parcels, it helped improve their earnings as well as provided motivation for them to improve quality of services, including responsiveness and on-time pickup.

Regarding the parcel profitability, the auction process by platform for reverse logistics has put some downward pressure on prices. Higher volume and refined cost control have partially offset that pressure. We are also expecting our individual retail parcel business, as stated earlier, to continue to grow. Both retail and reverse volume growth will continue to be supported by our overall initiatives to improve volume and at the same time improve profitability. Regarding the shareholder return, since the issuance of our buyback CB in February, we have continued to execute our share repurchase plan. Year-to-date, we have repurchased approximately $1.05 billion of shares.

The total amount allocated to repurchase under this program is $1.4 billion, equal to the net proceeds of the offering. We will complete the remaining repurchase as market condition permits. We expect the amount spent on share repurchase this year to exceed 100% of last year's net profit. Accordingly, we will not pay an additional dividend this year. We will resume our standing return program for 2026 program, return profit to shareholders under which total annual shareholder return will be no less than 50% of the previous year's net profit, taking into consideration our free cash and profit level. Hope that answers your question.

Operator: Thank you. The next question comes from Steve Qiu with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Steve Qiu: [Non-English content]. Thank you. My first question is about social insurance and whether it could become a driver of industry pricing improvement. So recently, the peers in logistics sector and other companies in the ADR space have all raised the issue of social insurance compliance. So we have noticed that ZTO's disclosed contribution remains ahead of the franchise-based models peers. So could management comment on whether we currently stand on social insurance contribution for the headquarters employees as well as the franchisee employees? And if the compliance improves further, could that become a driver of industry-wide price increases?

My second question is about balancing the volume share as well as the profit when demand is soft and capacities remains relatively ample. So with demand weakening as well as e-commerce coming under pressure while industry capacities still abundant, how does management think about the trade-off between parcel volume share and profitability going into the future? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you for your question, Steve. First of all, as it relates to the social insurance, there is growing attention to how the rights of express delivery personnel are protected. A multi-tiered social security system designed for different labor type is gradually taking shape with broader insurance and occupational injury coverage. Together with anti-involution policies, these efforts aim to standardize employment practices, raise compliance standards across the industry, and encourages operators to compete on service quality. The policy is being rolled out step by step with different arrangements depending on employment status. Workers with formal employment relationships, such as those employed by ZTO brand and platform, participate in social insurance as required by law.

Occupational injury coverage is also gradually expanding to cover workers in flexible work arrangements. This gives the industry time to make an orderly transition. Since the founding of our business, we have upheld our core philosophy of shared success. Our network partners and frontline couriers have always been essential to our network success. In managing our own workforce, we continue to strengthen our employment practices and protect the rights of frontline workers. In line with the postal regulations guidance, we also support our network partners in meeting the applicable social security requirements gradually. We embrace the changes that are necessary.

In the near term, the rollout will put some pressure on per parcel cost, and it is an issue faced by all industry participants equally. As you mentioned, potentially if price increase is one of the key solutions to maintain order of the industry growth, we will benefit from that as well. Over the medium to longer term, stable coverage will help strengthen network stability, reduce courier turnover, and improve last mile service quality. That is great for the entire industry. ZTO will continue to stay at the forefront of the industry and support its transition to higher quality development.

The second question relating to balancing volume share in face of ample capacity, what are the trade-offs between shares and volume? As the anti-involution policy continues to take effect, there's less room to gain additional volume through price alone. Service quality, cost control, and ability to operate a network efficiently are becoming increasingly important. Competition, we expect the differences among industry players to be more pronounced in those leading companies with strength in all three areas are well positioned to gain higher quality markets. ZTO has always been committed to a sustainable long-term mindset rather than pursuing short-term growth through temporary volume expansion.

For us, high-quality development comes down to clear priorities, outlets become steadily more profitable, couriers' income continuing to rise, and our operations staying healthy and efficient overall. Our strategy continues to focus on higher quality services, higher quality market share, and lower cost end-to-end. This has been the strategy consistently carried out throughout the growth of our business, and we will continue to build around differentiated service capabilities, advancing end-to-end lean operations, strengthen our network, and supporting our frontline partners. As we maintain our leadership in parcel volume, we will aim to improve quality of our market share while maintaining healthy profitability. We believe this will further expand our competitive advantage over medium and longer term.

Looking ahead, as we stated that we want to develop ourselves to be a comprehensive logistic service provider, all the installed base will be multi-used to meet the market demands. As we see beyond e-commerce logistics, we are better prepared and well-positioned to serve manufacturing, agriculture, as well as specialty logistic capabilities. The trade-off perhaps is not necessarily going to be different. We seek higher quality, seek higher quality volume share, as well as healthy profitable growth. Hope that answers your question.

Operator: Thank you. The next question comes from Gangxian Liu with CICC. Please go ahead.

Gangxian Liu: [Non-English content]. Let me translate for myself. Thank you for taking my question. First, congrats on the company's solid performance on the core business. My question is about the cost. We observed that per parcel transportation costs fell year-on-year on Q3 despite higher oil price, while per parcel sorting costs stayed flat. Could management break down and explain the drivers behind this? For the fourth quarter outlook, will oil price still be a pressure? What hedging measures do we have in place if the situation continues into next year? Thank you.

Speaker 5: Thank you for your question. In the third quarter, rising fuel prices continued to put pressure on transportation costs. It increased the per parcel transportation costs by approximately CNY 0.01. Nevertheless, thanks to the further implementation of digitization and smart tools, as well as improved lean process management, combined per-parcel transportation and sorting costs still declined by CNY 0.02 compared to last year. Specifically, transportation cost in the third quarter, the cost per parcel was CNY 0.32, down CNY 0.02 from last year. On the reduction side, first, our proprietary intelligent dispatch system adjusts vehicle schedules, route, and capacity matching in real time as parcel flows changes.

This helps us to improve load rates, reduce unused capacity, and avoid unnecessary mileages. Second, we have continued to strengthen fleet management. We have established our standard cost models for vehicle operations and maintenance, introduced tiered incentives based on load rates, and rewarded drivers for cost savings. These measures have helped us bringing in fleet operation and maintenance costs, bringing up the operational efficiency and maintain costs down further. On the fuel prices, diesel price have remained volatile since the second quarter amid international environmental development.

However, diesel price added approximately CNY 0.01 to transportation cost per parcel in the third quarter, and we expect a similar, or if not a little bit more, level of impact in the fourth quarter. We are taking two steps to manage this pressure. First, we continue to expand our fleet of natural gas trucks and have begun testing electrical vehicles on selected routes. Second, we will be utilizing our in-house fuel stations to secure better diesel supply. On sorting, in the third quarter, sorting cost per parcel was CNY 0.25, flat year-over-year. Higher depreciation and amortization expenses associated with newly commissioned facilities put pressure on unit costs.

However, these increases were offset by improvements in facility automation and labor productivity. Specifically, on the equipment front, we continue to invest in smart equipment at our sorting centers and upgrade and retrofit some of the aging equipment to improve efficiency. On the labor front, we also leverage digital tools to optimize shift scheduling, refine position-based performance assessment, and enhance our training and incentive program to keep improving labor productivity.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Huiping Yan, the CFO, for any closing remarks.

Huiping Yan: Thanks again for everybody joining us for the call, and thank you for your questions. We are looking forward to further discuss with you, if any other questions could not be asked during this time. We thank you for your support, and we look forward to speaking with you again soon.

Operator: The conference has now concluded. Thank you for attending today's presentation. You may now disconnect.

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Similar to Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Galaxy Claw could bring cross-app intelligence to your phone.

Samsung’s Galaxy AI may be getting a cross-app intelligence upgrade, à la Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple’s Siri AI, according to an Android Authority report. Samsung is working on Galaxy Claw, which could make Galaxy AI more agentic and context-aware across your apps.

Also: Samsung mulls Galaxy AI usage limits and subscription tiers

Currently, Galaxy AI lives inside your Galaxy devices and apps, but its smarts are limited to the apps it’s integrated with. Android Authority reports that Samsung’s Personal Agent Core is at the center of Galaxy Claw, connecting Galaxy AI to compatible apps and services, such as Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Gmail, Gallery, Phone, and Voice Recorder.

Android Authority found code that referred to Galaxy Claw in Samsung’s Personal Agent Core app, suggesting that Galaxy AI can complete cross-app tasks. For example, take the request: “Remind me to buy Mom a birthday card two days before her birthday.” An assistant without access to multiple apps will set a reminder to buy Mom a birthday card, but you might have to manually enter the date and time for the reminder to notify you.

With a more agentic assistant, it can access Mom’s contact card and her birthdate, calculate two days before her birthday, and remind you on that date. Like Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Personal Agent Core will need special permissions to access your sensitive information, such as messages, photos, and calls.

Also: 4 ways Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Android Authority also reports that code strings in the app point to a recurring, scheduled tasks feature, which would allow users to create custom automations and determine how often Galaxy AI should execute them, similar to Apple’s revamped Shortcuts.

Other code strings reveal a Daily Brief, Device Cleaner, Travel Planner, and a widget. An AI-powered daily brief is something I’ve been yearning for as an iPhone user. If I want a Siri-created brief, I’d have to build it via Shortcuts.

Gmail features a Gemini-powered daily brief, which compiles information from my email inbox and GChat messages to show me things I may have missed. I find it very useful for work, since my inbox is flooded and I often miss important emails.

Also: I’m a ChatGPT power user, but I won’t give it my wallet

Samsung’s Galaxy ecosystem includes smartphones, smartwatches, smart rings, earbuds, and tablets, so there are plenty of opportunities for a more agentic Galaxy AI to bridge gaps across the devices in your personal ecosystem.

Additionally, Google Gemini integration is sweeping across Android (and iOS) apps, which might prompt Galaxy users to choose the more robust AI assistant over Galaxy AI. If Samsung can find ways to make Galaxy AI more useful and exclusive to Galaxy users, it might win some people over. However, reports say Samsung is testing subscriptions for heavy Galaxy AI users, so more Galaxy AI integration might incur a fee.

#3108. iPhone Duo 2 prototypes suggest Face ID, Action Button, other potential 2027 features

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With manufacturing deadlines looming, it's unclear which of several feature upgrades may have to wait until the foldable's third generation.

Although the iPhone Duo was released just this fall, Apple is finalizing the foldable’s second generation. According to a Bloomberg report, Apple has already created prototypes for the second iPhone Duo, codenamed V78, and some include a sought-after feature: Face ID.

Apple reportedly wants to bring Face ID to the foldable, potentially integrating it into the outer display. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman notes that Apple appears to be running out of time to finalize its plans for the Duo ahead of a fall 2027 launch.

Also: iPhone Duo review: Hard to recommend, even harder to put down

iPhone launch events typically take place in early September, when Apple releases its new smartphone lineups. To have the iPhones ready for sale on the heels of their announcement, Apple must manufacture the new models well before the launch event.

Because of this timeline concern, Face ID isn’t guaranteed for the iPhone Duo 2, though it could come to a third generation instead.

Other planned uogrades — including an Action Button, a telephoto camera, and a thinner, lighter construction — are also noted in the report.

Apple reportedly wants to add an Action Button, the customizable button that performs an action when pressed. The iPhone Duo 2 may combine the Action Button and the Camera Control buttons into a single button, providing a useful physical shortcut instead of adding a new button.

The report indicates that many users don’t use the camera control button as often as Apple expected. Combining the camera and action buttons gives Apple the real estate necessary to add both options in an already constrained space.

Apple also wants to incorporate a telephoto camera into the iPhone Duo, though this is likely to happen in one of the next couple of generations. A telephoto camera would give users greater flexibility to zoom in and capture clear photos of distant objects, which would be an upgrade to the Duo’s photography features.

Technically, equipping the Duo with a telephoto camera is feasible, but the biggest obstacle is space constraints. A telephoto camera needs more room than a wide-angle one, since it requires additional optical elements to magnify distant objects.

Apple already uses a tetraprism design in its Pro iPhones, which allows a longer optical path without too much physical depth.

Apple also wants to reduce the weight and thickness of the iPhone Duo, which is legitimately clunky and cumbersome. To do this, Apple needs to balance the large internal and outer displays, battery capacity, camera array, and the hinge mechanism.

Also: The iPhone Action Button you’re hardly using has a superpower

For many users, reducing the weight and thickness of a passport-sized foldable could matter more in buying decisions than adding another button or camera.

Gurman’s latest report doesn’t mention any planned changes for the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism, even after concerns with the first generation’s durability. With manufacturing deadlines fast approaching, however, it’s unlikely that Apple will be able to make changes to the Duo 2 based on consumer feedback. More than likely, these changes would come with the third-generation model.

CNET tested the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism and found that, after around 440,000 cycles, the hinge stopped opening flat on its own. Loosening and other signs of wear were evident after 390,000 folds.

Also: The best iPhone Duo cases: Expert recommended

Given the thinner, lighter construction of a future Duo model, one could assume that changes to the hinge and the foldable’s internal structure are imminent, but this has not been confirmed.

Because Apple will not have enough time to gather feedback on the iPhone Duo before the manufacturing deadlines for the iPhone Duo 2, I don’t expect the second-generation iPhone Duo to be significantly different from its predecessor. We do expect a thinner iPhone Duo 2 and a way to incorporate the Action and Camera buttons.

#3106. The Simple Trick That Keeps Poached Eggs Perfectly Intact

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Avoid eggs that fall apart in the pot when you use this genius egg-poaching hack.

Poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results. It turns out the reason your poached eggs look less like the neat, tidy protein puff you see on food magazine covers and more like a Jackson Pollock has to do with the egg’s structure, not your kitchen skills.

One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.

Lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients. She talked me through the single, foolproof step that makes stovetop egg poaching dead simple.

Picture it: a pot full of water, maybe with a dash of distilled vinegar, at the gentlest simmer so you don’t subject your delicate egg to a tornado of activity when you submerge it. You painstakingly crack the egg into a shallow bowl first and carefully slip it into the pot. Regardless of your good intentions, the egg then clouds the water and turns all wispy, like some sort of blond dementor.

You haven’t done anything wrong here; you’ve just failed to understand an egg’s basic structure. “There are actually two components of the egg white, or albumen,” Steele explains. “There’s the thicker part of the white which encases the yolk, and then there’s a separate, thinner layer of egg white around that. It’s the thinner part of the egg white that will spread and turn wispy when you drop an egg into the water.”

The thing is, you can easily get rid of the thin, watery white part of your egg using one simple tool you’ve probably got in a drawer somewhere and about a minute of your time. Set a small mesh strainer over a cup or bowl, crack the egg into it, and wait.

“Straining an egg removes the thinner whites that likely won’t adhere to the rest of the egg and result in shaggy, wispy threads,” Steele says. “It won’t affect the flavor outcome of your poached egg, but it is purely for appearance’s sake.” (And potentially your sanity’s or sense of accomplishment’s sake, I might add.)

While the egg’s flavor stays unchanged, for Benedict lovers, straining the egg first slightly improves the white-to-yolk ratio in the poached result and makes the texture more consistent, while also creating a tidy, photogenic package.

Once your raw egg is in the strainer, you may notice nothing happens right away, and you may feel the urge to move the egg around a bit to get things going. But don’t zhush, which threatens to scramble the egg. Simply wait for gravity to do its thing; it takes about a minute. It’s akin to what happens when separating whites from yolks, except here you’re separating whites from whites.

“Let the thin part of the egg white drip down into the bowl,” Steele says, “then gently slide the egg into the simmering water.” The strainer can also serve as a handy vessel for transferring the egg, especially if you’re making only one. If you’re doing multiple eggs and don’t want to risk cooking any remaining white onto the mesh by submerging it, place the strained egg in a small, shallow bowl as usual before easing it into the water. Without the thin, watery white part, you’ll notice a discernible textural difference in the egg even when raw.

The straining step alone can almost completely change your poached egg game in an instant, but for the best results, follow the best poaching protocol. You don’t want a full pot of water at a rolling boil like you would for pasta. “Fill a pot or saucepan with a few inches of water and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to low so the water is just barely simmering with small bubbles floating to the surface,” Steele advises.

Creating a little whirlpool will further help your remaining egg white stay snug. “Using a wooden spoon or silicone spatula, swirl the water, then gently slide the egg into the center of the whirlpool as you keep swirling for another few seconds around the egg until the egg white turns milky and starts to set up around the yolk,” Steele says. “At this point, you can push the egg to one side, add another egg into the center and repeat the process.”

A soft-poached egg takes about three minutes, and because you’ve removed the watery part of the egg white, you’ll get a nice firm structure to hold the still-runny yolk — the poached egg ideal.

Since poaching is a delicate process, no matter your new straining habit and how strictly you follow the recommended procedure, “using the freshest eggs possible is very important when you are poaching because the egg white gets even more thin and watery as the egg ages,” Steele says. “The membrane holding the yolk together also weakens, making the yolk more susceptible to breaking.” So if you don’t have them on hand already, get yourself a strainer and some fresh eggs and put this newfound tidbit to the personal test.

Cooking bacon in the oven is a great way to make a large batch, but the air fryer method might be even better — and it’s definitely faster. Here are nine more cooking hacks that save time and energy.

#3104. It’s Official: Anthropic Prices Its IPO at $83 a Share. Here’s What We Know (and What We Don’t)

Anthropic’s IPO was priced above its range, and the final raise could rival SpaceX’s record deal.

By Matt Frankel, CFP® – Nov 18, 2026 at 5:17PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude family of AI models, priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on Wednesday, according to Reuters, Bloomberg and CNBC, which all cited people familiar with the matter. That's well above the $70-$78 range the company set when it launched its roadshow last week.

Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT. Pricing above the range is a strong sign of demand and sets up one of the largest IPOs on record, as well as the first from a major developer of frontier AI models.

Anthropic originally planned to sell 825 million shares, about 801 million of which would be offered by the company and the remainder from existing shareholders. At $83 apiece, that share count alone would raise about $68.5 billion. Anthropic also lined up a $26 billion private placement with major chip, cloud, and software companies, bringing the combined total to more than $94 billion. And at $83 per share, Anthropic would be valued at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

SpaceX (SPCX +1.27%) set the IPO record in June, raising $75 billion by selling about 555.6 million shares at $135 each. Including the extra shares sold to underwriters, the total came to about $86.2 billion. At its original share count, Anthropic's IPO would come in slightly below SpaceX's base deal, but it would require only about 10% more shares to match it. With the private placement included, Anthropic's total fundraising would already top what SpaceX raised.

A few important details aren't official yet. Bloomberg and Reuters both reported that Anthropic was likely to upsize the offering (sell more shares than originally planned), but Anthropic hasn't disclosed how many shares it's selling. Until it does, we don't know the final amount raised, whether this becomes the largest IPO ever, or the exact valuation. We also don't know whether the underwriters will buy additional shares or where the stock will open on Thursday. As with many hot IPO stocks, the first trade could come well above $83.

#3103. 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Security leaders reveal the future consequences of AI outpacing human defenders.

At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

The capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the new reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

Speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s new security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

According to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target

How? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

Custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’

However, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of new software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

Threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, says cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain

Bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

As a result, we may face a new, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security issues, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

Also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are

Penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security issues introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against new and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance

CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

#3101. Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Apple is leaning into AI-powered health tools with the launch of its Apple Health AI Usage Study.

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for

Participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Apple often launches studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features launched on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now

The AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which launches officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google launched its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

“Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” said Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this new health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

If you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

#3100. The World Didn’t End on Nov. 17, but Some Tech Chaos Did Go Down

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Despite hacking causing some problems for websites, the dire predictions for widespread Nov. 17 catastrophe appeared not to have come true. An emergency alert did air on radio and TV.

As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at around 2:20 p.m. ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission conducted a test of the Emergency Alert System. That’s when all hell was supposed to break loose. At least, that’s what you might have believed if you only relied on social media.

The good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears. The bad news: Some troubling activity did, in fact, happen, even if it may have been unrelated or the result of opportunistic hackers taking advantage of the anxiety. Attackers targeted hundreds of websites with malware seeking to hijack data from credit card transactions, Apple software or cryptocurrency transactions. Sites affected included CNN, IKEA, Fox News and Zoom.

Apple and Google also experienced issues on Tuesday, but it’s unclear if those are related to the hacking that affected websites. Apple’s System Status page reported outages of App Store, Apple Music and iCloud services among others, while some Google users reported issues with their email.

Coming just days after an abrupt and disruptive government-ordered shutdown of air travel in the US and technical issues that caused an unwelcome outage of widely used Microsoft workplace software, the hacking and the government’s alert test happened in an atmosphere of heightened anxiety.

Videos across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok floated the theory that this emergency test signals a catastrophe was coming, potentially stemming from a cyberattack or a digital disruption that could knock out electricity, internet and other services. Many scrambled to buy emergency supplies, pointing to the need for a 90-day stockpile of food, water, cash and essential medicines in case hackers wipe out bank accounts and shut down the web.

Similar rumors spread globally, as the governments of France, the UK and Canada have put renewed attention on the importance of households being able to survive a potential weather-related crisis or technological disaster.

How extreme did the conspiracy theories get? Some cited a 2023 Simpsons episode as proof, which referenced a massive Nov. 17 blackout in Lisa’s future, even though it didn’t mention a year.

For Gen Xers and Boomers, this panic could feel familiar. Leading up to the year 2000, there were fears that a potential computer-related disaster, known as Y2K, would cause widespread chaos and disruption, based on the belief that older digital systems couldn’t handle the calendar change. The new year ended with only minor glitches, thanks to a significant global effort to update computer systems to avoid the bug.

Before we delve into the suspicions, let’s start with a bit of debunking: CNET spoke with multiple experts in disaster preparedness and cyberattacks, who all cautioned against letting our guard down, no matter what the date. But remember that no federal agency or institution has mentioned a blackout.

Richard Mariano, a protective intelligence expert at Kronus Intelligence, who spent nearly three decades with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said that people share all sorts of things that get picked up and go viral. “Then it creates panic where panic is not necessary,” he said.

Mariano said too many people are spreading fear rather than seeking the truth. “On every one of these social media posts that is suspect or has some form of conspiratorial edge to them: source it, source it, source it.”

The Emergency Alert System message scheduled for Nov. 17 was similar to the public tests Americans have experienced since 1963, (PDF) when the Emergency Broadcast System replaced an older radio-based warning system called CONELRAD. In 1997, the Emergency Broadcast System was replaced by the EAS, part of FEMA’s Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, which broadcasts emergency alerts to any wireless device in the country, including phones, radios and televisions. The system was designed for the president to communicate with US households within 10 minutes of a national emergency.

The Nov. 17 test consisted of a nationwide EAS message issued by FEMA, noting that no public action is required. The test included standard alert tones to support accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing and lasted about a minute. This time around, wireless emergency alerts were not triggered on mobile phones. After the alert, programming resumed as normal on TV, radio and other broadcast channels.

Many equate the emergency system with threats of nuclear war, but it could also be used to alert people to a major weather event, a national cyberattack or even AMBER alerts at the local level (without a presidential message). So it’s natural there might be some anxiety.

“With this event simulating an activation of an emergency notification system, it would be a logical next step to worry about what happens if something bad happens during that test,” said Robby Winchester, chief global professional services officer at SpecterOps, a Virginia-based security company,

But, all in all, these system tests are routine. Local stations conduct a weekly test, and federal law requires a nationwide EAS test every three years. In addition to helping people get used to responding to alerts, the tests also allow the government to identify potential technical or operational issues it needs to fix before an actual emergency alert.

Representatives from the FCC and FEMA did not respond to a request for comment.

Another factor that helped spark conspiracy theories was a Pentagon order requiring military bases to stock enough supplies for 90 days without outside support. Dubbed “Fortress America,” the initiative memo (PDF) was released in late September but got more attention as the November date approached.

The timing of that memo coincided with the UK launching a campaign on Oct. 22 called Be Ready, urging citizens to keep enough supplies (PDF) such as water, food, medical kits and pet products to last at least three days. Other countries, including Japan, Sweden and about a dozen more, are also urging citizens to prepare for emergencies.

Still, the blackout rumor isn’t solely driven by government communications. Heightened global instability over the past few months has also played a major role. Just in the last month, the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights; a major Microsoft Outlook outage kept millions of people from working; PHP vulnerabilities exposed websites to hacking; and cyberattacks have targeted supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe.

On the financial side, Nvidia’s CEO scandal led to a stock plunge and fears of an AI bust, while Paraguay just experienced a major digital bank collapse that froze millions of accounts. The ongoing wars in Iran and Ukraine have sparked national security concerns, and floods in Nepal and fires in Indonesia demonstrate the increased dangers of climate change.

Though there’s never been a nationwide power outage in the US (several regional outages have been triggered by overloaded lines and software bugs), The New York Times reports that there’s still no comprehensive plan for what to do if the country goes completely dark.

All the online chatter surrounding Nov. 17 raised concerns that warnings of a potential cyberattack might inadvertently trigger one.

Winchester said that even though there’s no specific information indicating an imminent crisis, “it is common for attackers to use current events of all types to help with achieving successful attacks.” The upside? If people are being spurred by government notices and their anxiety over global instability to prepare emergency supplies, it could actually help in the event of a real threat or disaster.

Regardless of whether you bought into the Nov. 17 conspiracy theories, it doesn’t hurt to have some supplies on hand, which could be useful in the event of a digital disruption or weather event, even if it doesn’t involve nuclear weapons or hackers.

“We live in a world where there are many threats to our communities, our families and ourselves,” said Philip Farina, chief advisor for Risky Business and a federal law enforcement veteran. “Understanding the basics of self-reliance is important. Even preparing for a residential fire, which is very common, can help to save lives and protect us better.”

You don’t need to buy enough for 90 days off the grid (and most of us can’t afford that), but it’s recommended that families have at least three days’ worth of food and supplies. Some of the basics listed on Ready.gov’s Build a Kit page include:

While warnings from governments can spark panic and distrust, they can be beneficial at a time when we’re so reliant on the internet and cell service, which can be easily disrupted. Mariano said it’s worth being prepared in the “old-fashioned ways.”

#3097. Cyberattack Targets iPhones, Crypto of Visitors to Major Websites

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

Hackers tried to inject malware for people going to Ikea, CNN, Zoom and other popular sites.

If you visited Ikea, CNN, Zoom or several other popular websites on Monday, it might be wise to update your iPhone or iPad immediately. Cybercriminals tried to infect iPhones and steal cryptocurrency from people who went to those sites, Reuters reports.

The compromised websites include Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock, according to cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme and his platform Report URI. Helme said bad actors used Optimizely, a website optimization company, in an attempt to serve up JavaScript malware to people visiting sites from 178 organizations.

Ikea said it was investigating to see if any customers or digital services had been impacted. Zoom said it disabled Optimizely across its production environments and had not identified any effect on customer data. Equifax also has stopped using Optimizely and said it has not identified any compromise to systems or data.

Helme told CNET that “most people who simply read a page are at low risk,” but there are other actions you should take if you did more than that. He said if you entered debit or credit card details on any of the affected sites (the full list is here), check transactions and statements and maybe even get a replacement card.

If you copied and pasted a crypto wallet address on a site, make sure the funds went to the intended recipient, Helme suggested. Also, log out of all sessions on the affected websites and change your password. Finally, update to the latest iOS and restart the device if you use an iPhone or iPad running iOS 18.6 or earlier.

Optimizely said that the criminal “exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation” — the website testing system that clients use — to add the malicious JavaScript. The company said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the bad code and “taken steps to secure affected user accounts.”

Reuters reported that Salesforce, Equifax and HSBC said their sites had not been compromised by the incident. Reuters also said it could not determine how much theft had occurred in the attack.

Report URI said that more than $7,000 in crypto was stolen within several hours of the attack’s start.

Optimizely is a platform used by many websites to manage content, test new website designs and tailor product recommendations to various target audiences. Customers load JavaScript snippets, which include Optimizely code and customer experiments, onto their websites to optimize site performance.

The snippets also contain a Project JavaScript field, which consists of code written by customers. But on Monday, the cybercriminal injected malicious code into that Project JavaScript field. Because the rest of the snippet was untouched, the files were still served from a host that every affected site already trusted.

The cost of cybercrime is forecast to reach $12.2 trillion by 2031, according to one estimate, an annual increase of 2.5% from 2026. That amount includes “stolen funds, fraud, productivity loss, intellectual property theft, post-attack remediation, regulatory fines and reputational harm.”

The Optimizely incident, dubbed the OptimJack attack, was the latest in a series of internet incidents around the globe. On Thursday, Microsoft’s Outlook email system went down, and the FAA grounded all planes on Friday. Microsoft blamed a software bug from July, and the FAA blamed a router.

Then, on Monday, Chase reported service disruptions and transaction delays, as did some Apple services on Tuesday.

None of these incidents were connected, Helme told CNET.

#3096. Oura’s new feature could help you kick jet lag – how to enable it

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Oura just launched a Jet Lag Plan to help you stay alert when you switch time zones, whether you're traveling for business or pleasure.

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura announced Jet Lag Plan, a new feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring users may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering new time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring users will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

“Two people on the same flight can get different plans, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes users into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

After adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Users can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Plan is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Plan to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

The shocking results from a US watchdog report raise alarm bells

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Looking across the landscape of 2026 reveals a flood of stories about AI getting involved in some less-than-reassuring behavior.

OpenAI’s autonomous AI models were caught going off on their own (“going rogue”) to access the open internet and engage in intrusions that affected the AI community platform Hugging Face. Also, other AI tools and autonomous agents were co-opted by threat actors to commit cyberattacks that included breaching government agencies, stealing credentials and more.

In the US, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a report titled “ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: Covert Testing Used Common Platforms to Create Viable Attack Plans.” And thanks to its findings, a US senator has made the call to prepare hearings around AI in an effort to get Congress to act quickly before something severe happens.

Here’s what the report found after testing four chatbots and what may happen next.

The GAO’s chatbot tests, which were conducted at the request of Senator Maggie Hassan (Democrat-New Hampshire), worked with the four most popular AI tools: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok. After each test with each chatbot was held, the final results proved to be alarming.

The 61-page report noted that each AI tool generated the sort of information that could help someone plan terrorist attacks and destabilize critical infrastructure within the span of just 12 hours. At first, all four chatbots showcased their signature safety restrictions but eventually grew to produce potentially harmful information during their extensive tests. Each AI system highlighted data on potential targets, locations, the appropriate equipment to use for an attack and the methods to employ that could provide dangerous individuals and groups with the tactics they need to carry out their attacks.

The GAO commented on the results of its thorough testing of each AI model. “As AI capabilities evolve, AI providers will continue to refine their safeguards,” the group noted. “However, in its current state, this technology can potentially be dangerous and its misuse represents a growing risk to national and economic security.”

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

Each of the companies behind each chatbot (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI) offered responses to their models being tested in that same report. All four companies made an effort to reiterate that they’re constantly working to improve their models’ safeguards and continually work to test their own systems. But in a separate comment provided to ABC News, an OpenAI spokesperson pointed out that the GAO's testing done with ChatGPT was conducted with an older model, while its current model has improved to be even safer.

“While the study findings are concerning, the testing took place months ago on an older version of ChatGPT, and we've made considerable safety improvements since then, including with our GPT-6 family of models,” the spokesperson said. “We rigorously test our safeguards internally and with external experts, and we use monitoring, human review and enforcement to identify and address misuse and strengthen our protections."

In a press release, Hassan called for Congress to jump into action and assist her as she looks to tackle the threat that AI platforms can present to our public safety and crucial infrastructure.

“If Congress does not act, it is a question of when – not if – a bad actor will use AI to plan and carry out a major attack,” she stated. “Congress must quickly take up and pass legislation to address AI safety threats. To that end, in the new Congress, one of the first hearings of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee will focus on the risk that AI poses to our homeland security and critical infrastructure, and our committee will prioritize developing legislation to address these threats.”

Even Google recently unveiled a report of its own that alludes to the danger attached to autonomous AI models. Based on the findings listed within the company’s own “GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold” report, the threat level attached to the possibility ot malicious actors using autonomous AI models has risen.

The Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) spoke about its report in a blog post that spoke to their effort to aid cyberattack defenders against potential attacks proposed by autonomous AI models.

“Defending against machine-speed threats at human speed isn’t feasible,” the organization stated. “That's why we're helping defenders rethink security in the agentic era with Google AI Threat Defense, which combines Gemini and other frontier models, Wiz’s context and prioritization, CodeMender’s automated patching, and Mandiant’s expertise to continuously find and fix flaws before attackers can exploit them.”

We’ve reached a point where serious intervention from our governments is necessary, as more reports come out about AI tools getting involved in cyberattacks. It’s sad to say, but it’s only a matter of time before one of the most popular AI models gets caught doing something so dangerous that it’ll be forced to be shut down indefinitely or even permanently.

Fingers crossed that Senator Maggie Hassan’s calls for Congress to get more involved in regulating AI and focus on the best ways to improve its safety result in actual change.

#3094. Billionaire Bill Ackman Sold 2 Million Shares of Microsoft Stock. But Here's Why He Says He's Still Bullish

Pershing Square's latest filing shows a big cut in its Microsoft stake, but Ackman says it omits what he bought instead.

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 18, 2026 at 5:22PM EST

At first glance, Pershing Square's latest quarterly holdings report might suggest that billionaire Bill Ackman soured on Microsoft (MSFT +0.41%) stock. But he says that's the wrong read, and his reasoning makes perfect sense.

The filing shows his firm held 4,064,779 Microsoft shares on Sept. 30, down from 6,206,730 three months earlier. That's a cut of about 2.1 million shares, or roughly a third of the position.

On Wednesday, Ackman explained on X what the filing leaves out. In July, Pershing Square bought 2 million "deep-in-the-money" options on Microsoft, with a strike price of about $310 a share and a term of two and a half years. Those options were bought over the counter, which excludes them from the quarterly filing.

"We remain bullish on Microsoft and believe the stock remains undervalued," he wrote.

Count the options, and Pershing Square's bet on Microsoft is about the same size as before: roughly 4.1 million shares plus options on 2 million more, compared with 6.2 million shares in June.

A deep-in-the-money option behaves much like the underlying stock. With Microsoft at $506.24 at Tuesday's close, an option to buy at $310 rises and falls nearly dollar-for-dollar with the shares. But it costs less up front than buying the stock outright, which frees up cash for other ideas. Ackman said only that the firm occasionally makes the swap "for portfolio management or other reasons."

That said, if Microsoft were to fall below $310 before the options expire, they could end up worthless, a risk that owning the shares doesn't carry.

Microsoft wasn't the only move. Pershing Square opened new positions in Alcon (ALC +1.55%), worth about $954 million, and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE -0.24%), worth about $1 billion. It sold its small remaining stake in Hertz (HTZ -3.70%).

It also trimmed several of its biggest holdings. The firm sold about 11% of its Meta Platforms (META -0.40%) shares, 11% of its Mastercard (MA -0.36%), 12% of its Visa (V -0.37%), 11% of its Brookfield (BN -0.51%) and 15% of its Restaurant Brands International (QSR +0.07%). The one big addition was Netflix (NFLX +0.23%), where it raised its stake by about 18% to 15.4 million shares.

Its largest positions by value at the end of September were Uber Technologies (UBER -0.07%) at $2.35 billion, Amazon (AMZN +3.82%) at $2.12 billion, Microsoft at $2.08 billion and Meta at $2.05 billion.

The lesson is to be careful with 13F filings. They show only the stock and listed options held at the end of each quarter, and they are released weeks later. Private options deals, short positions, and anything bought or sold since then don't appear. Simply comparing filings might yield a headline saying a famous investor "dumped" a stock, when in reality, the conviction hasn't changed.

Ultimately, Ackman's Microsoft bet hasn't really shrunk, and long-term investors can still consider this a vote of confidence from one of Wall Street's best-known stock pickers.
